Subject: Observability add-ons — need a clear cost split for retention/tracing/dashboards

Hi Rishi / Marissa,

Thanks again for the overview last week. Procurement asked me to get a clear line-item view of how Redwood prices the observability add-ons so we can budget and move this through our SOW approval. We’re looking to understand two things: a) how you break out fees between retention (log storage), tracing (span ingest & storage), and advanced dashboards, and b) what discounts you can offer with a 12-month committed contract and a pilot period up front.

To make the ask concrete, here are our approximate monthly numbers from a recent pilot:
- Ingested logs: ~350 GB/month (compressed)
- Retention target: 90 days (we may need 180 for a subset)
- Tracing: ~1.2M spans/day 
- Dashboards: 12 power users, ~60 viewers
- Current objective: production rollout in Q1 if price + controls align

Specific questions:
1) Do you price retention per GB-month or as a flat slab? Are archival tiers cheaper?
2) How do you bill tracing (per span, per 1M spans, or by retention window)?
3) Dashboards — do seats matter or do you offer seatless org-level bundles?
4) If we commit to 12 months and a baseline commit (TBD), what discount ranges are typical? Any credits for pilot months?

I attached our procurement template (procurement_template.pdf). Can you reply with a ballpark spreadsheet and recommended packaging options? Procurement wants an itemized view they can plug into their SOW.

Sam
Sam Tully
Director, Observability & SRE Programs
Magellan Health

Subject: Re: Observability add-ons — need a clear cost split for retention/tracing/dashboards

Hi Sam — thanks for the details, that’s very helpful. I pulled together an initial, ballpark pricing matrix (attached: pricing_matrix_v1.xlsx) and a short narrative below to explain the line items. This is intended to be a starting point for Procurement and your engineering stakeholders.

High-level (monthly, USD, ballpark):
- Retention (hot storage): $0.20 per GB-month for the first 1TB, moving to $0.12/GB-month beyond (tiered). Archive (30–90 day cold tier) available at $0.04/GB-month. For your 350GB and 90d target, estimate ~350 * 0.20 = $70/month for hot + modest archive at scale.
- Tracing (ingest + retention): $8 per 1M spans ingested, plus $0.05 per 1k spans-month retained beyond 7 days. For 1.2M spans/day (~36M/month) the ingest charge would be ~36 * $8 = $288/month; retention depends on your window — I can model 30/90/180 days in the spreadsheet.
- Advanced dashboards: Two options — seat-based ($45/user/month for power users) or seatless bundle ($2,000/month for up to 100 viewers and 20 power users). For 12 power users + 60 viewers the seatless bundle often gives better predictability.

Discounting and pilot:
- 12-month commit: standard discounts are 10% for annualized usage >= $50k, 15–20% for larger multi-year commitments.
- Pilot credits: we typically offer a 3-month pilot with up to $15k in usage credits for trials that convert to committed purchase. For this opportunity, I can propose a pilot credit of $10k if Procurement signs a Letter of Intent within 30 days.

Packaging recommendation (based on your numbers):
1) Start with a seatless dashboards bundle + metered retention and tracing.
2) Offer a 3-month pilot (credits applied to retention + tracing) to validate retention windows and trace retention costs.
3) If you commit to 12 months at conversion, apply a 10% baseline discount; we can model higher discounts on committed $/month thresholds (I show scenarios in the spreadsheet).

Next steps: 1) I’ll loop in Irene to draft a SOW outline and a pilot scope, 2) if Procurement is happy we’ll follow with a draft SOW and a DocuSign path. Any details you want modeled (e.g., which services require HIPAA controls or special retention partitions) let me know.

Attaching: pricing_matrix_v1.xlsx (line-item estimates).

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra

Subject: Re: Observability add-ons — need a clear cost split for retention/tracing/dashboards

Sam — quick follow up from the delivery side. I’m including a few practical notes so the SOW maps cleanly to billing and security needs.

1) Retention packaging: we recommend metered credits against a monthly GB budget for the first phase so you don’t get hit by bursty ingress. Metric: commit to a baseline GB/month + pay-as-you-go overage at the same per-GB rate. For the subset needing 180d retention, we can create a scoped archival bucket with a lower rate and explicit lifecycle rules.

2) Tracing: we bill ingest and retention separately. For long windows (90–180d) we suggest keeping summarized spans (sampled) beyond 30 days to control cost — we can automate sampling policies as part of the rollout.

3) Dashboards: Seatless bundle requires a minimum 12-month contract; if you want month-to-month we’ll do seat-based billing at the per-user rate.

SOW items I’ll include in the draft: pilot scope (3 months), success criteria (ingest stability, 95th-pctl query latency, dashboard adoption), data partitioning and HIPAA controls, rollback/fallback plan, and an initial acceptance test. I’ll attach a draft SOW to the next message.

Requested from you: can Procurement confirm if a 10k pilot credit is acceptable to cover ingestion/retention costs during the POC? That will speed approval.

Best,
Irene Choi
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Rishi / Irene — that spreadsheet is exactly the kind of line-item view Procurement wanted. A few quick replies from Procurement:
- They like the metered-credit approach for retention rather than a large slab up front.
- The 3-month pilot with a $10k credit sounds reasonable; Procurement asks if we can cap monthly spend during the pilot so internal stakeholders don’t get surprises.
- They also want the SOW to call out HIPAA handling and an audit trail for retention policies before signing.

Procurement asked me to confirm we’re good to proceed with a pilot once we get a draft SOW and a DocuSign link. Please send the SOW and indicate whether the pilot monthly spend can be capped (we’d prefer a hard cap of $6k/month during the pilot, with overage requiring an explicit approval).

If you can get the SOW and DocuSign to me this week, we’ll try to process LOI approvals on our side.
